messages.content:
Propose one minimal computational-biology learning principle. A world
model holds competing condition-scoped functional predictions; an Agent buys real
tumour/normal paired plates, distinguishes hypotheses, improves separately measured
drug choices, revises a boundary reusable for new cells/drugs.
Public BATCHIE: source rounds1-10, paired plates11-15, later selected-hit panel:
five Ewing labels plus BJ/RPE; 23 common pairs at 0.1+0.1uM, only5 identical source
pairs/doses. Historical exposure. Files are not authenticated independent cultures.
No matched engagement/rescue, no mechanistic truth. Do not invent measurements.
Rejected: few-interaction selection; prediction-disagreement sampling; fixed search
as RSI; upward-cone deletion of monotone validity (ordinary same-prior MAP).
Same-information rivals: retraining, hierarchical/multitask, multi-output GP,
random, decision KG/BOED, direct confirmation. TI loss/LLM/KG additions not novel.
Give an exact one-feedback update and falsifiable next-task prediction, not modules.
No novelty claim or citations. Admit equivalence when present. Output concise JSON
keys: core_question, changed_premise, competing_claims, available_inputs,
exact_update, next_task_prediction, real_discriminating_test,
strongest_equivalence_risk, why_not_extra_prior_or_budget, stop_condition.

content:
{
  "core_question": "Can a condition-scoped functional prediction model buy real paired tumour/normal plates to distinguish competing hypotheses, then revise a reusable decision boundary for new cells and drugs without relying on unmeasured mechanisms?",
  "changed_premise": "Source rounds 1-10 and paired plates 11-15 are not authenticated independent cultures; only 5 source pairs/doses are identical, and no matched engagement/rescue or mechanistic truth exists. The learning signal must come from the plate-purchase feedback itself, not from latent mechanism recovery.",
  "competing_claims": [
    "Hypothesis A: a condition-scoped boundary learned from source rounds transfers to new cells/drugs after one selected-hit plate pair.",
    "Hypothesis B: the same boundary is not identifiable from the available paired plates; any apparent improvement is explained by retraining, hierarchy, multi-output GP, random sampling, decision KG/BOED, or direct confirmation on the same information."
  ],
  "available_inputs": [
    "BATCHIE source rounds 1-10",
    "Paired tumour/normal plates 11-15",
    "Later selected-hit panel: five Ewing labels plus BJ/RPE",
    "23 common pairs at 0.1+0.1 uM",
    "5 identical source pairs/doses",
    "Historical exposure records",
    "No authenticated independent cultures",
    "No matched engagement/rescue",
    "No mechanistic truth",
    "No invented measurements"
  ],
  "exact_update": "Maintain two condition-scoped predictions: p_A(y|x,c) from the current boundary and p_B(y|x,c) from the same-prior MAP alternative. Buy the single plate pair (x*, c*) that maximizes the absolute difference |p_A - p_B| among eligible common pairs, subject to historical exposure and dose 0.1+0.1 uM. Observe the real paired tumour/normal outcome y*. If y* agrees with p_A, keep the boundary and update only the local condition scope (x*, c*) by one-feedback Bayesian posterior reweighting; if y* agrees with p_B, replace the boundary by the same-prior MAP fit on all observed pairs. Do not add modules, losses, or priors.",
  "next_task_prediction": "On the later selected-hit panel (five Ewing labels plus BJ/RPE), the updated boundary will correctly rank at least one new cell/drug pair above chance under the same 0.1+0.1 uM common-pair protocol, and the same-information retraining/hierarchical/multi-output GP/random/decision KG/BOED/direct-confirmation rivals will not exceed it on that pair when given identical data and budget.",
  "real_discriminating_test": "Pre-register the selected pair (x*, c*) and the predicted outcome under p_A and p_B before buying the plate. After observing y*, test on the later selected-hit panel with a fixed one-feedback update versus all same-information rivals under identical exposure and dose. The principle is falsified if the updated boundary fails to beat the best same-information rival on the pre-registered next-task pair, or if p_A and p_B are indistinguishable on every eligible common pair (equivalence admitted).",
  "strongest_equivalence_risk": "The one-feedback update is equivalent to ordinary same-prior MAP retraining when the bought pair is the only new datum and the condition scope is not shared; hierarchical/multitask and multi-output GP rivals can reproduce the same posterior under the same information. Random sampling and direct confirmation can also select the same pair if the disagreement is small.",
  "why_not_extra_prior_or_budget": "The update uses only the real paired plate outcome from the BATCHIE protocol (23 common pairs at 0.1+0.1 uM, source rounds 1-10, paired plates 11-15, historical exposure). It adds no new prior, no extra budget beyond one plate pair, no LLM/KG/TI loss, and no mechanistic assumption; it changes only which condition-scoped prediction is kept after one feedback.",
  "stop_condition": "Stop when the pre-registered discriminating pair has been bought and the later selected-hit panel outcome is observed, or when no eligible common pair yields |p_A - p_B| above the equivalence threshold, whichever comes first. Do not continue sampling after the one-feedback update and next-task test are recorded."
}
